basis: Decision 0017 and docs/wire/routing.md. A link carries addressed values (decision 0015) whose message is the routing record (bitwire/routed/1, origin, payload). Encoded bytes are hand-derived from ontos-codec-v1 (Atom=00 length bytes, Tuple=01 arity items) with the 19-octet addressed header and the 16-octet record header, then checked against the released 0.5.0 encoder. The reject and decision expectations precede any routing implementation. Atoms are hex.

observations: Every hop sends the addressed value it received unchanged: the same destination, origin and payload bytes. Decode then encode of each encode vector reproduces its bytes.

A binding receives messages under the generation it was installed with. After release or replacement, a message that arrived on the earlier generation is refused as stale-binding and is never forwarded through the replacement.
Releasing a generation that is not current changes nothing. A link's termination removes only the binding of that link's generation.

Binding a key that has a live binding is refused; so is a second parent, a parent at the root, and a link whose receive slot is already owned. The binding limit refuses further bindings without affecting existing ones.
Messages arriving on one link are decided in arrival order, and those forwarded to the same next link keep that order. Nothing is promised between different arriving links.
A refused forwarding send on the next link is reported as not-admitted; while a next link is closing, either not-admitted or, once its release is observed, missing-route is correct.

Every refusal observation carries the refused payload unchanged, for every reason including not-admitted, so the host can act on the exact value even though the router owns the receive slot. Nothing is sent on any link because of a refusal.
A value on a link that is not an addressed value carrying a routing record fails that link through handler failure, as for the addressed facade. Payloads are never decoded.
Routing adds no queue. Releasing the router detaches its receivers and refuses its own sending; it closes no link.
